title: Brain training shows promise for short-term depression relief | New Scientist
description: Training that encourages people to alter their brain's activity seems to reduce negative emotions among people with depression, but not in the way researchers expected
author: Sascha Brodsky

title: Cells from your mother could stay in your brain your whole life | New Scientist
description: Most people seem to have cells that crossed the placenta from their mother into their developing brain in utero, even if they're now in their 80s
author: Chris Simms

title: The land's ability to store carbon has bounced back after two bad years | New Scientist
description: Carbon absorption by forests and grasslands bounced back in 2025 thanks to favourable growing conditions, but El Niño could lead to another sharp slump next year
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Why the worst El Niño killed millions – and how we can avoid a repeat | New Scientist
description: The world hasn't experienced an El Niño this strong since the 1870s, when it sparked a terrible global famine. Are we better prepared this time?
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Two large asteroids found spinning as fast as a fairground ride | New Scientist
description: Rocks in the asteroid belt rotating at ultra-fast speeds suggest our understanding of asteroid structure might be wrong
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan

title: Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? | New Scientist
description: Most covid-19 cases are caused by a particular type of variant, but do we need to worry every time a new one emerges?
author: Jo Marchant
